emb:L2042453206.model_family: 2.5D deep learning model (ResNet-18 with transfer learning on multiplanar CT reconstructions)
emb:L2042453206.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing CT for craniofacial trauma
emb:L2042453206.model_description: Axial, coronal and sagittal CT reconstructions are stacked as a three-channel input to a ResNet-18 convolutional network with transfer learning to flag pediatric craniofacial fractures. The pipeline includes isotropic resampling, bone-window normalization and 384x384 image generation; Grad-CAM highlights the regions driving each prediction, which an independent clinical review confirmed corresponded to fracture-related structures.
emb:L2042453206.headline_result: AUC 0.822, AUPRC 0.855; at optimal threshold (t=0.54): sensitivity 0.556, specificity 1.000, F1-score 0.714
emb:L2042453206.study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L2044216298.model_family: 3D U-Net and attention-based CNNs for ventricular segmentation; SVM, random forest, XGBoost and RNN/LSTM for prediction
emb:L2044216298.clinical_problem: predicting timing of neurosurgery and prognosis in congenital hydrocephalus
emb:L2044216298.patient_population: children with congenital hydrocephalus, with MRI, CT and CSF biomarker data
emb:L2044216298.model_description: MRI and CT images from children with congenital hydrocephalus were segmented with 3D U-Net and attention-based CNN architectures to automate ventricular measurement. Clinical and CSF biomarker features (after KNN imputation and PCA) were combined with the imaging findings and fed into machine learning (SVM, random forest, XGBoost) and deep learning (RNN, LSTM) models to stratify risk, predict disease progression and evaluate surgical outcomes; explainable AI identified ventricular enlargement, CSF dynamics and periventricular changes as the top predictive features.
emb:L2044216298.headline_result: test accuracy exceeding 95% with high precision, recall and F1-scores; XGBoost outperformed traditional classifiers, LSTM best predicted longitudinal progression

emb:L2044564684.patient_population: 30 normal singleton pregnancies, 28-36 weeks of gestation
emb:L2044564684.model_description: 4D ultrasound recordings of fetal facial movement (blinking, mouth movements, grimace duration) are planned to be analyzed with the VISAGE|SDK AI tool, which estimates emotional states and their variability, and correlated with Kurjak Antenatal Neurodevelopmental Test (KANET) scores to assess whether facial movement patterns reflect fetal neuromuscular development. This is a prospective study protocol; the abstract reports anticipated, not actual, results.

emb:L2044564684.study_design: prospective observational study protocol (results not yet reported)

emb:L2045268571.model_family: multitask deep learning (EfficientNetB4-based classification and regression)
emb:L2045268571.clinical_problem: skeletal (bone) age assessment for growth and developmental disorders
emb:L2045268571.patient_population: children undergoing hand radiography for bone age assessment (RSNA pediatric bone age dataset)
emb:L2045268571.model_description: Hand radiographs are fed into an EfficientNetB4-based multitask model that jointly performs classification of developmental stage and regression to estimate bone age, with a gender-based input representation, a six-layer validation framework, a three-layer safety mechanism, and a confidence estimation module for clinical decision support. The model was trained on the public RSNA pediatric bone age dataset.

emb:L2045426934.model_family: deep learning (classification, segmentation and automation methods; architectures not specified)

emb:L2045426934.model_description: This literature review (2019-2025) surveys deep learning methods applied to obstetric ultrasound, covering classification of normal versus abnormal fetal anatomy, segmentation, and automated fetal biometry, aimed at reducing operator dependency and interpretation variability in prenatal imaging.

emb:L2045804035.model_family: radiomics (LASSO feature selection) combined with logistic regression
emb:L2045804035.clinical_problem: predicting postnatal outcome of congenital pulmonary malformation detected prenatally
emb:L2045804035.patient_population: 100 fetuses with congenital pulmonary malformation detected on prenatal ultrasound and confirmed after birth
emb:L2045804035.model_description: Radiomics features were extracted from targeted prenatal grayscale ultrasound images of fetuses with congenital pulmonary malformation and reduced with LASSO regression to a radiomics score. This score was combined with an independent clinical predictor (congenital pulmonary airway malformation volume ratio) in a logistic regression model to predict postnatal outcome.
emb:L2045804035.headline_result: AUC 0.809 (combined model) vs 0.728 (clinical model) and 0.770 (radiomics model) in the test set

emb:L2045804044.exclusion_reason: general review of pediatric cardiovascular MR/CT technique for low-sedation, low-dose imaging; AI mentioned only as a future outlook, not evaluated

emb:L2045804052.model_family: deep learning (unspecified architectures) for feature extraction from fetal brain MRI
emb:L2045804052.clinical_problem: assessing fetal brain development and detecting neurodevelopmental abnormalities
emb:L2045804052.model_description: This review covers AI methods, primarily deep learning, applied to fetal cranial MRI: predicting gestational and brain age, detecting structural abnormalities such as sulcal and ventricular changes, and assisting motion correction and analysis of fetal functional MRI data, with the aim of building AI into clinical decision support for early diagnosis and intervention.

emb:L2045855042.clinical_problem: image acquisition guidance and diagnostic interpretation support in pediatric point-of-care ultrasound
emb:L2045855042.patient_population: children in emergency and critical care settings undergoing point-of-care ultrasound
emb:L2045855042.model_description: This review discusses AI-assisted models for point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in pediatric emergency and critical care, noting that AI can improve image acquisition and augment training, which is particularly useful where ultrasound experts are scarce. It cautions that models trained mainly on adult populations require pediatric-specific validation before use, and that AI should supplement rather than replace ultrasound training and credentialing.

emb:L2046115581.headline_result: ensemble models reported AUC 0.85-0.92 for predicting CKD/ESRD progression from kidney ultrasound

emb:L2047827159.clinical_problem: quantitative assessment of chronic rhinosinusitis severity (sinus volume and inflammatory involvement)
emb:L2047827159.patient_population: pediatric patients undergoing CT for chronic rhinosinusitis
emb:L2047827159.model_description: A 3D convolutional neural network was trained to automatically segment the maxillary sinuses on pediatric CT scans, using manually annotated expert segmentations as ground truth, then compute sinus volume and the percentage of the sinus affected by inflammatory changes, giving a quantitative alternative to descriptive CT scoring of chronic rhinosinusitis in children.
emb:L2047827159.dataset_size: 92 CT scans of the paranasal sinuses in pediatric patients
emb:L2047827159.headline_result: mean sensitivity, precision and Dice coefficient near 90%; root-mean-square error 0.4 cm3 for sinus volume and 1.3 percentage points for inflammatory involvement
emb:L2047827159.study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L2048461360.clinical_problem: AI-assisted prenatal ultrasound and fetal MRI interpretation, including standard-plane recognition, image quality assessment, fetal biometry, fetal cardiac screening, and prediction of growth restriction, preterm birth and preeclampsia
emb:L2048461360.patient_population: fetuses undergoing prenatal ultrasound and MRI
emb:L2048461360.model_description: This narrative review (literature from 2021-2026) summarizes AI applications in prenatal medicine. The strongest evidence supports AI-assisted standard-plane recognition, image-quality assessment and fetal biometry on ultrasound, with emerging evidence for fetal cardiac screening, blind-sweep ultrasound, fetal MRI segmentation and placental phenotyping, and for predicting fetal growth restriction, preterm birth and preeclampsia. Most applications remain limited by retrospective design, enriched datasets and insufficient external validation; the authors recommend a human-in-the-loop model with prospective validation before autonomous clinical use.

emb:L2048461366.model_family: deep learning CNN with multiscale feature extraction, channel-wise attention, and edge-aware loss
emb:L2048461366.model_description: PMSAN classifies chest radiographs as pneumonia or normal, combining multiscale feature extraction and channel-wise attention with a novel edge-aware loss function to sharpen detection of subtle pathology. It was trained and evaluated on the public Kermany pediatric chest X-ray dataset, with interpretability supported by ROC curves, attention maps and edge maps.
emb:L2048461366.headline_result: test-set accuracy 96.4%, precision 97.9%, recall 97.2%, F1-score 97.6%, AUC 0.988; five-fold cross-validation accuracy 96.4% +/- 0.5%, AUC 0.988 +/- 0.003, outperforming ResNet18 and VGG16 baselines
emb:L2048461366.study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L2048537432.clinical_problem: AI applications across pediatric imaging, with bone age assessment and chest radiograph interpretation as the most established use cases
emb:L2048537432.model_description: This narrative review examines why pediatric imaging AI differs from adult radiology AI, citing developmental variability, different disease epidemiology, imaging constraints, and limited pediatric datasets. It finds the most mature applications are in image acquisition, dose reduction and workflow optimization, with bone age assessment and chest radiograph interpretation the most established interpretive/prognostic use cases, while adult-trained models often underperform in children. It calls for pediatric-specific design, shared data infrastructure, federated learning, and age-stratified prospective validation.

emb:L2034313518.model_description: A YOLOv10-based object detector, enhanced with AC-BiFPN for multi-scale feature fusion, a SimAM attention module to emphasize clinically relevant image regions, and a WIoU loss function to reduce both false positives and false negatives, was trained to detect fractures on pediatric wrist radiographs from the public GRAZPEDWRI-DX dataset, intended as a real-time decision-support tool for emergency departments.

emb:L2035493833.model_family: EfficientNet (B0/B1/B2) CNN with SVM and KNN classifiers
emb:L2035493833.clinical_problem: diagnosis and Graf classification of developmental dysplasia of the hip
emb:L2035493833.patient_population: 947 infants (450 girls, 497 boys) undergoing hip ultrasound, January 2018-September 2021
emb:L2035493833.model_description: Hip ultrasound images were classified with EfficientNet convolutional neural networks (B0, B1, B2 variants), without manual image annotation, first into normal (Type 1) versus dysplastic hips, then into four Graf sub-types based on the alpha angle. Support vector machine and k-nearest neighbor classifiers were layered on top of the CNN features to further improve accuracy.
emb:L2035493833.headline_result: accuracy 0.9577 (EfficientNetB1) for 2-class classification and 0.8571 (EfficientNetB0) for 4-class classification; with added classifiers, up to 0.99-1.00 (2-class) and 0.97 (4-class)

emb:L2039031939.model_family: dual-encoder CNN segmentation network with boundary feature enhancement and channel recalibration modules
emb:L2039031939.clinical_problem: segmentation of pneumonia-infected lung regions on chest CT in children
emb:L2039031939.patient_population: children with pneumonia undergoing chest CT
emb:L2039031939.model_description: A dual-encoder deep learning network segments pneumonia-infected regions on pediatric chest CT. A boundary feature enhancement module uses prior contour labels and multi-directional edge detectors with cross-attention to sharpen lesion boundaries, while a channel recalibration module suppresses background noise, together improving segmentation of small, low-contrast infected regions; the network also generalized to adult COVID-19 CT images.
emb:L2039031939.headline_result: Dice, Jaccard index, sensitivity and Matthews correlation coefficient improved by 2.99%, 4.76%, 2.56% and 3.03% respectively versus the best-performing comparison network on pediatric pneumonia CT

emb:L2039419962.model_family: 3D diffusion and symmetrical attention-based frequency-domain adaptive global feature network (DSA-FAGFNet), CNN-based
emb:L2039419962.patient_population: children undergoing head/orbital CT for suspected orbital fracture
emb:L2039419962.model_description: PIOFSF is a deep learning pipeline for screening pediatric orbital fractures on CT: it performs 3D reconstruction, corrects for head tilt so the orbits are symmetrically aligned, localizes the orbits using clustering and a Hough transform, then classifies fracture presence with a 3D network (DSA-FAGFNet) combining diffusion-based orbital position coding, symmetrical attention and frequency-domain feature extraction, aiming to catch subtle fractures that are often missed or misdiagnosed as other conditions in children.
emb:L2039419962.study_design: retrospective technical development / diagnostic accuracy study

emb:L2039917384.model_family: machine learning and deep learning (SVM and CNN most common)
emb:L2039917384.clinical_problem: diagnosing ADHD and predicting treatment response using neuroimaging and clinical data
emb:L2039917384.model_description: This systematic review of 147 studies (through October 2024) covers machine learning and deep learning methods, most often SVM and CNN, for diagnosing ADHD and predicting response to pharmacological and non-pharmacological treatment. Inputs include clinical/demographic data, cognitive tests, and neuroimaging or electrophysiological modalities (EEG, fMRI, structural MRI, MEG, DTI, SPECT, fNIRS, PET). Reported diagnostic accuracy reached up to 99.95% with EEG signals and up to 92.8% with combined structural and functional MRI, while far fewer studies addressed treatment-response prediction.
emb:L2039917384.headline_result: diagnostic accuracy up to 99.95% with EEG signals; up to 92.8% with combined structural and functional MRI

emb:L2041377376.model_family: deep learning (U-Net variants, transformer-based models, CNNs, implicit neural representations)
emb:L2041377376.clinical_problem: detecting fetal neurodevelopmental abnormalities via automated analysis of fetal brain imaging
emb:L2041377376.patient_population: fetuses across a wide range of gestational ages, imaged with MRI and ultrasound (55 studies synthesized)
emb:L2041377376.model_description: This systematic review of 55 studies (2005-2025) covers deep learning applied to fetal brain MRI and ultrasound: brain segmentation and regionalization (the largest share of studies), structural measurement, image reconstruction/enhancement/synthesis, and predictive/classification modeling, using architectures including U-Net variants, transformers, CNNs and implicit neural representations. It proposes a federated learning framework with explainable AI and synthetic data generation to address data diversity, privacy and interpretability gaps identified across the reviewed studies.
emb:L2041377376.dataset_size: 55 studies; individual study datasets ranged from 753 to 433,000 images
